“Racialized” is used throughout this resource. Employment equity sources use the category “members of visible minorities”. PSES racial identities and employment equity self-identification use different definitions. Indigenous identity is measured separately. Differences between groups can identify questions for examination; they do not, on their own, establish discrimination.

ISC representation history

Who is included in these figures?

TBS counts indeterminate employees, terms of three months or more, and seasonal employees in the core public administration. Students, casuals, short terms, employees on leave without pay, and certain appointees are excluded. Racialized representation is based on voluntary self-identification. The published expected count is retained; it is not recalculated from rounded percentages.

Subgroup counts and shares

02

Applicants, hiring and advancement

Explore PSC data for ISC. A share of appointments measures the composition of staffing activity. It is different from an individual employee’s probability of promotion.

ISC staffing records

The PSC source supplies applicants for 2025–26, while its other measures run through 2024–25. Applicant counts, hires and employee populations have different bases and cannot be used as a selection funnel. Acting appointments cover four months or more. PSC and TBS populations differ: for 2024–25, PSC reports 1,758 racialized ISC employees; TBS reports 1,759 as of 31 March 2025.

ISC survey explorer

How to interpret the survey measures

“Agreement / selected response” uses the source AGREE field. It reports agreement with statements, “yes” to yes/no questions, or selection of a response option. For questions about the extent of an effect, it includes any reported extent. A higher value can describe either a better experience or more harm, depending on the wording. Read the full question and response base beside each row.

“Favourable” and “unfavourable” retain the publisher’s MOSTPOS and MOSTNEG summary measures. PSES summary measures can exclude “Don’t know” and “Not applicable”. Raw response percentages use different bases. Response counts are rounded and vary by item. A missing or suppressed value is never converted to zero.

The “non-racialized” and “White” survey groups are distinct. Racial identity choices can overlap. Racialized executives’ survey results describe respondents; they are not executive representation counts.

Branch comparisons

05

PSC staffing survey results

Explore the 2023 and 2025 Staffing and Non-Partisanship Survey for ISC, including visible minority groups and subgroups. The questions and eligible populations differ between cycles.

Published response distribution

Weighted results and eligible respondents

The PSC publishes weighted response shares and weighted response counts. A weighted count is not the number of people who completed the survey. Percentages here are the published share multiplied by 100, without reweighting or removing “Don’t know”. Each question may apply only to managers, staffing advisors, applicants, or respondents with a particular experience. Multi-select response percentages may sum to more than 100%.

The 2025 survey covers experiences from 1 April 2024 to 31 March 2025 and was administered from June to August 2025. It is separate from PSES 2024. Missing subgroup rows mean that the reviewed source does not supply that selection.

Data coverage and remaining questions

Five annual ISC snapshots from 2021 to 2025, departmental availability, expected counts, and published racialized subgroup breakdowns.

Staffing and employee experience

PSC applicants, hires, promotions and acting appointments; 2024 PSES comparisons and 11 ISC branches; 2023 and 2025 PSC staffing survey distributions.

Questions for further data requests

ISC racialized representation by EX level and feeder group; salary distributions; selection rates through the same hiring processes; and reasons for separation. These breakdowns were not identified in the sources assembled here.

For network discussions, record the exact population, question, reporting period and source with each finding. A representation gap is different from a survey gap. A share of promotions is different from a promotion rate.

Contact ARAN about a data question

07

Sources and methods

Figures come from published Government of Canada data, with ISC extracts assembled from the source files and related ARAN data resources.

Preparation and verification

ISC records were extracted from the GC Equity data archive in Google Drive and the ISC equity and PSES branch repositories. The current TBS representation and subgroup tables and the current PSC employment equity CSV were retrieved directly from their publishers. PSES department records retain EEINFODV.csv values, with overall results from main-principal.csv. Branch records retain the EELEVEL2ID values. The downloadable extracts preserve published suppression markers.

Ten connected GitHub repositories were reviewed for relevant sources. National-only salary, executive and imputed figures were excluded from ISC-specific measures. The full inventory and source revisions are available in sources.json.

Accessibility and privacy

This site uses semantic headings, labelled form controls, keyboard-accessible navigation, visible focus indicators, text descriptions and tables for charts, responsive layouts, and reduced-motion support. Every main function is available in English and French. It uses no analytics, tracking cookies, accounts or personal-data submission form. Language choice is stored only in your browser. Contact links open your email application.
